dispositions.topic_text: Who computes the submission digest and how the public contract guarantees the same procedure as confirmation generation
Whether confirmation binds raw, normalized, or semantically equivalent input values
Which canonical typed encoding and digest construction binds confirmation inputs unambiguously
dispositions.what: The canonical typed encoding and the digest of the confirmation binding: one procedure in owner_sessions (_confirmation_binding_digest) used at the step and at the submission; action, target, version, then every field of the inputs in its model's order, each list in its order, absent told apart from empty; a collision-resistant cryptographic digest.
keeps:
A pending confirmation shown for one action, target, version and inputs
    is refused, and used up, when the submission carrying its value changes
    any one of them: another action, another target, another version or
    none, another value of any input, or the same list in another order
    (rule 6).
options: Use a domain-separated typed length-prefixed encoding with an order-sensitive cryptographic digest.
Use canonical JSON with fixed rules for types, absence, numbers, Unicode, object keys and array order.
Use a dedicated ordered encoder for each confirmed action.
consequences: A typed binary encoding is unambiguous but requires shared encoding machinery.
Canonical JSON is inspectable but requires complete canonicalization rules.
Action-specific encoders are explicit but duplicate logic and may drift as actions evolve.

dispositions.topic_text: Whether digest equality defines confirmation binding or collision-disambiguating/injective binding is required
dispositions.what: Whether digest equality defines the binding: _confirmation_binding_digest is a collision-resistant cryptographic digest of one unambiguous encoding, so distinct inputs never share an encoding and a collision is the digest's, not the design's; the values are never kept.
options: Define binding by digest equality and accept colliding inputs as equal.
Retain collision-disambiguating information without retaining the input values.
Require an injective digest over the admissible input domain.
State that digest collisions are outside admissible histories.
consequences: Digest equality weakens the literal differing-input guarantee if collisions are admissible.
Collision-disambiguating or injective binding preserves the absolute mismatch guarantee but constrains the retained representation.
Excluding collisions requires an explicit assumption defining admissible histories.
